notes:
Account summary: Orchid Signalworks is a legaltech ISV building an internal RAG search product for law firms + corporate legal. Heavy index (targeting 30M-50M documents initially), strict residency + retention requirements. Currently using in-house BM25 + monoBERT reranker; exploring embeddings + cross-encoder reranker migration to improve precision on long legal clauses.

Recent timeline: 
- 2026-01-14: Intro call (AE Maya Chen) — high-level goals, expressed cost sensitivity and latency SLOs.
- 2026-02-05: Technical deep-dive with SE (Oliver Park) — provided 45M sample index, query distribution, p95 target.
- 2026-02-24: Demo + Q&A (Fireflies: ffx_2026-02-24_orchid-rag-demo). Walked through Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization + batching.
- 2026-03-03: Security review kickoff; exchanged security FAQ and SAML metadata.
- 2026-03-05: Pricing + procurement sync; finance asked for ARR estimate and PO cadence.

Use-case & requirements (short):
- Workload: enterprise search for contracts, precedents, litigation notes. Embeddings + reranking primary.
- Index scale: 30M initial, plan to grow to ~150M over 18 months. Need efficient incremental indexing, compaction.
- Latency targets: p50 <= 70ms for embeddings-only recall, p95 end-to-end <= 250ms for reranker flow at 100 QPS burst.
- Throughput target: steady 100 QPS, spikes to 350 QPS during month-end research windows.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost/per-query <$0.002 (avg) — must demonstrate batching/kv-cache savings.
- Model preferences: prefer open models; evaluating 1536-d embeddings -> 768-d candidate for cost reduction; reranker migration from monoBERT -> lightweight cross-encoder (quantized).
- Quality guardrails: cannot accept recall/precision regression vs current monoBERT baseline. Need eval-driven migration with A/B and canary.

POC & acceptance criteria:
- Run Redwood-provided eval harness across 12k benchmark queries (legal prompts) comparing current stack vs Redwood embeddings+reranker.
- No >1.5% drop in normalized nDCG@10 and recall@50 across key verticals.
- End-to-end p95 under 250ms at 100 QPS in dedicated environment.
- Cost projection report showing >=25% reduction in per-query cost at target load.

Migration plan (preferred):
- Phase 0: Snapshot indexing + offline eval (2 weeks) — run 45M snapshot through embedding pipeline, collect metrics.
- Phase 1: Canary A/B (10% traffic) for 2 weeks with automated eval calls; monitor quality regressions; rollback policy defined.
- Phase 2: Gradual roll to 50% then 100% with canary-aware routing and model-variant fallbacks (region-aware).
- Post-roll: continuous eval set + alerting for regressions; monthly quality baseline re-calibration.

Operational/tech asks:
- Embedding versioning + ability to pin index -> must support replay/rehash.
- Native support for per-route model rollouts (canary + A/B).
- Token-level cost visibility and per-query breakdown.
- KMS integration for keyring (HSM optional).
- Audit logs for inference requests, retention controls 7y (legal requirement).

Open questions & blockers:
- Can Redwood produce deterministic eval reports tied to our legal prompt sets (we need reproducible metrics for procurement)?
- Data residency: need EU-only storage for certain clients (some entities require EU-only).
- Budget: procurement window opens 2026-04; need final pricing + SLA to land in Q4 contract.

Customer quotes / call snippets: 
- "If we see a measurable drop in precision on clause matching we can't ship — quality is everything." — Head of Product
- "Cost per query needs to be demonstrably lower at scale; otherwise the migration is a net negative." — VP Eng

Next steps (short):
- Deliver detailed POC plan + cost model (owner: Maya) by 2026-03-12.
- SE to provision dedicated test stack for 45M snapshot and enable eval harness (owner: Oliver).
- Security to finalize SAML/KMS scoping; Leah to coordinate CSM handoff post-contract.
